nodes.summary: Let $f(n)$ be the least number of colours in a $(4, 5)$-colouring of $K_n$, that is, a symmetric colouring of the pairs of vertices of $K_n$ in which the six edges of every $K_4$ receive at least five distinct colours. Then $f(n)/n \to 5/6$ as $n \to \infty$.
nodes.title: Erdős Problem 136: the $(4, 5)$-colouring number of $K_n$ is asymptotically $5n/6$

nodes.summary: Let $f(n)$ be the least number of colours in a $(4, 5)$-colouring of $K_n$. This is the proposition that $f(n)/n$ tends to $5/6$ as $n \to \infty$; equivalently, $f(n) = (5/6 + o(1))\, n$.
nodes.title: The asymptotic of the $(4, 5)$-colouring number (Erdős Problem 136)

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$, $f(n)$ is the least natural number $k$ such that $K_n$ has a $(4, 5)$-colouring with $k$ colours; such a $k$ always exists.
nodes.title: The $(4, 5)$-colouring number $f(n)$

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $n$ and $k$, the complete graph $K_n$ on the vertices $0, 1, \dots, n - 1$ has a $(4, 5)$-colouring with $k$ colours if there is a map $c$ assigning to every ordered pair $(x, y)$ of vertices one of $k$ colours, with $c(x, y) = c(y, x)$ for all $x, y$, such that for any four distinct vertices the six edges between them receive at least five distinct colours.
nodes.title: $(4, 5)$-colourings of $K_n$

fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
